from jobs import unique_jobs

def test_basic():
    rows = [
        {'title': 'job1', 'source': 'A', 'source_id': '1'},
        {'title': 'job1', 'source': 'A', 'source_id': '1'},  # duplicate same source/id
        {'title': 'job1', 'source': 'B', 'source_id': '1'},  # diff source
    ]
    res = unique_jobs(rows)
    # first occurrence of (A,1) kept, (B,1) separate
    assert len(res) == 2
    # first row (A,1) kept, second same removed
    # second distinct row (B,1) also kept
    titles = {r['title'] for r in res}
    assert titles == {'job1'}

def test_none_source_id():
    rows = [
        {'title': 'job1', 'source': 'A', 'source_id': None},
        {'title': 'job1', 'source': 'A', 'source_id': None},
        {'title': 'job2', 'source': 'A', 'source_id': None},
    ]
    # None source_id -> keep separately, not dedup
    res = unique_jobs(rows)
    assert len(res) == 3

def test_empty_source_id():
    rows = [
        {'title': 'job1', 'source': 'A', 'source_id': ''},
        {'title': 'job1', 'source': 'A', 'source_id': ''},
        {'title': 'job2', 'source': 'A', 'source_id': ''},
    ]
    res = unique_jobs(rows)
    # empty string also separate
    assert len(res) == 3

def test_missing_source_id():
    rows = [
        {'title': 'job1', 'source': 'A'},  # no source_id key
        {'title': 'job1', 'source': 'A'},
        {'title': 'job2', 'source': 'A'},
    ]
    # rows without source_id should be kept separately
    res = unique_jobs(rows)
    # all kept
    assert len(res) == 3

def test_stable_first_occurrence():
    rows = [
        {'title': 'job1', 'source': 'X', 'source_id': 'a'},
        {'title': 'job1', 'source': 'X', 'source_id': 'a'},  # dup
        {'title': 'job1', 'source': 'X', 'source_id': 'a'},  # another dup
        {'title': 'job1', 'source': 'Y', 'source_id': 'a'},  # diff source
    ]
    res = unique_jobs(rows)
    # first X,a kept, Y,a kept
    assert len(res) == 2
    # order should preserve first occurrence? stable dedup not reorder? requirement stable first occurrence wins.
    # we keep order of first appearance.
    # first row (X,a) appears first, second dup removed, third dup removed, Y row appears later.
    # So res should have rows 0 and 3.
    assert res[0]['title'] == 'job1' and res[0]['source'] == 'X' and res[0]['source_id'] == 'a'
    assert res[1]['title'] == 'job1' and res[1]['source'] == 'Y' and res[1]['source_id'] == 'a'

def test_no_mutate():
    rows = [
        {'title': 'job1', 'source': 'A', 'source_id': '1'},
        {'title': 'job2', 'source': 'B', 'source_id': '2'},
    ]
    rows_orig = rows[:]
    res = unique_jobs(rows)
    # original rows should not be mutated
    # ensure source_id not overwritten? function should not modify dict.
    # simple check that ids equal
    for i, r in enumerate(rows):
        orig = rows_orig[i]
        assert r['title'] == orig['title']
        assert r['source'] == orig['source']
        # source_id could be None/empty but shouldn't be changed
        assert r['source_id'] == orig.get('source_id', None)

if __name__ == '__main__':
    test_basic()
    test_none_source_id()
    test_empty_source_id()
    test_missing_source_id()
    test_stable_first_occurrence()
    test_no_mutate()
    print('all tests passed')
